fix: 'filaments' is mapped to stamen; PO has filament (PO_0009067), so 'filaments longer than X' should keep filament as bearer.
reason: The comparison is made of the filaments, not of the whole stamens; the towards slot (perianth) and the quality are right.
'Capsule ... hispid, rarely without hairs' = fruit rarely not hairy; negation and the 'rarely' qualifier have the right scope.

'Stem ... densely armed with slender straight prickles': the stem bears sharp outgrowths; spiny is the usual grounding of 'armed'. Strictly they are prickles, not spines, but PATO has no 'prickly' term.
'stamens about 25' = stamen count 25; the 'about' is not recorded as a qualifier but the value is right.

fix: In Paronychia sepal descriptions, 'awn ... with yellowish spine' describes the tip of the sepal awn; the colour should go on the awn (or its spine), not on the whole sepal.
reason: The sepals are not said to be yellow; only the spine that ends the awn is yellowish.
'stamens unequal, 2–3.6 cm, longer than corolla': the stamens are longer than the corolla.

The involucral bracts range in shape from linear to broadly elliptical; 'bract' and the continuum are right. The further alternative 'trisect and leaf-like' is left out, which does not make the statement false.
The leaf lobes are ovate to broadly triangular; bearer, quality and the continuum match.
'bracts ... 4-7 × 1-1.5 mm': the first figure is the length, 4–7 mm.

fix: In 'glabrous except ... pubescent on midvein below', the hairs are on the midvein (abaxial side), not the whole lower surface; when a vein is named before 'below/beneath', the vein should be the bearer and 'below' only the side.
reason: The blade is said to be glabrous except for hairs sometimes on the midvein underneath; 'lower blade surface pubescent' is false.
'Pseudo-ombelles: pauciflores' = few flowers in the inflorescence; flower present, amount few, container inflorescence.

fix: The spines of a Franseria/Ambrosia bur are outgrowths of the fruiting involucre, not thorns (PO thorn = a modified shoot). 'Spines' on fruits or burs should not map to thorn; there is no fitting PO term, so the bearer needs a better term or a rejection.
reason: The shape (somewhat conical) is right, but the part is the bur spine, not a stem thorn.

fix: 'sheaths ... not twisted' should keep leaf sheath as bearer instead of falling back to leaf.
reason: The 'not twisted' is said of the sheaths; the same text calls the scapes 'very slightly twisted', so the bearer matters.

fix: In flower descriptions, 'spur' means a nectar spur; it is wrongly matched to short shoot (synonym 'spur'). In orchids, 'lip' is the labellum, not corolla lip (FLOPO_0985017). PO has no nectar spur and there is no labellum class, so the item cannot be grounded now.
reason: Piperia: the floral spur is shorter than the labellum; neither the bearer (short shoot) nor the comparison target (corolla lip) is right.

fix: 'filaments ..., lateral pair 1.5-3.5 mm' should keep filament as bearer and record 'lateral pair' as position; otherwise it clashes with 'median pairs 2-4.5 mm'.
reason: The lengths are those of the lateral filaments, not of all stamens.
'Fronds ... not proliferous' = frond not proliferous; the negation is right.
'leaflets ... abaxially pilose' = the underside of the leaflets is pilose (leaflet is the outer bearer).
The leaf blade is black-brown when dry: brown, with the dried-specimen condition recorded.
'petiole ..., base sheathed': the leaf base is drawn out into a sheath, which is the definition of sheathing (FLOPO_0991105) for a leaf.
(1–)6–7+ dm = 60–70 cm, with an extreme minimum of 10 cm; converted right.
In Senecio, the anther appendages grow from the connective; their ovate-lanceolate shape fits the connective as bearer.
'leaflets ... puberulent beneath' = leaflet underside puberulous.

fix: Ideally 'above' should be scoped to the upper (adaxial) surface.
reason: The upper surface is pubescent or pilose; the underside is also pubescent, so 'leaf pubescent or pilose' is still true.
'usually densely hairy abaxially' = lower leaf surface hairy. The 'usually' is dropped but the statement is not false.
'Male flower with very numerous stamens' = stamens present, many. The male-flower context is missing, but female flowers are not said to lack stamens, so it is not false.

fix: Section headings like 'Pistillate inflorescences:' or 'Staminate ...' should fill the sex/state slot for every statement that follows, up to the next heading.
reason: Only the pistillate inflorescences are sessile or subsessile; the staminate ones have a peduncle 0.1–0.7 cm, so 'inflorescence sessile' without the context is false.
'Stems 25-150 cm, glabrous': the stem is glabrous.

fix: 'nervation en relief' (and 'nervures saillantes', 'veins raised') describes the veins; the rule should give the leaf veins as bearer, not the leaf.
reason: It is the veins of the leaf that are raised, not the leaf itself.
'Heads many, to ca. 80 per corymb' = capitulum present, many.
The '(basal)' figure is the lobe width of basal leaves: 5–30(–50) mm, with basal (FLOPO_0991002) recorded as context; the cauline value is a separate statement.
